correctness.rationale: PASS. For independent continuous X_1,...,X_n, a record R_i has probability 1/i, an interior peak P_j has probability 1/3; indicators are independent for i<=j-2 by disjoint observation sets and for i>=j+2 by independence of unordered prefix values from its uniform rank permutation. At i=j-1,j,j+1 the exact joint probabilities are 1/[(j-1)(j+1)], 1/(j+1), and 0, respectively, yielding the three displayed covariances after subtracting 1/(3i). The column sum is 1/[3j(j-1)(j+1)] and telescoping gives (n-2)(n+1)/[12n(n-1)] for every n>=3. Independent exhaustive exact-rational enumeration of every entry for n=3,...,7 agreed. The all-n argument, not the finite enumeration, proves the result.

originality.rationale: PASS only for the position-resolved kernel and its three-diagonal independence law. Ji (2023), following Carlitz–Scoville, supplies aggregate generating functions including interior peaks and record counts, so the displayed total-count covariance is prior-covered, not new. An aggregate bivariate enumerator has no position markers and does not determine individual (i,j) covariances. Resultary searches located record–excedance, record–fixed-point and cycle–peak kernels involving different event pairs, but no theorem establishing this exact record–peak matrix. Historical position-marked sources may exist.
